# Fetch drops request headers before native dispatch

## Context

Found while validating the existing Pipeline interceptor request, #9553, and independently triaged by Grace. The [retained probe](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/9553#issuecomment-6690092267) uses actual native HTTP: the same Authorization input reaches the endpoint through native `fetch`, but not through `Neo.data.connection.Fetch.request`.

## The Problem

At `cda4f4c385`, the endpoint observes no Authorization header, although `response.request.headers` still echoes the supplied value:

```json
{"nativeFetchHeader":"Bearer interceptor-probe","connectionFetchHeader":null,"requestCarrierHeader":"Bearer interceptor-probe"}
```

The method sends only body and method to native fetch. The existing `defaultHeaders` member is also unused by this dispatch. A metadata assertion therefore cannot certify a sent header. This defect exists without any interceptor configuration.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: the owning `Fetch.request` API exposes request configuration, its metadata spec describes the URL and headers a caller reads back, and Fetch declares `@member {Object} defaultHeaders=null`. The sibling HTTP connection, Xhr, already merges connection defaults with per-request headers. Native Headers semantics provide case-insensitive names.

Prescription checked: `src/data/connection/Fetch.mjs#request` owns native RequestInit assembly. `src/Fetch.mjs` inherits it for the public Neo.Fetch facade. Fixing Pipeline or adding middleware would leave direct consumers broken. Closed #19436 repaired URL metadata and explicitly excluded header/body support; #4553 addressed an undefined config, not dispatch headers.

## The Fix

Forward supplied headers at the native Fetch boundary in both URL forms. Honor the existing defaultHeaders member, with per-request values overriding matching names case-insensitively; preserve caller-owned header inputs. Keep URL resolution, method/body dispatch, response decoding and rejection envelopes intact. Add native HTTP and real App/Data-worker coverage.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Edge case | Docs | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fetch.request headers / defaultHeaders | Existing request config and defaultHeaders member | Native request carries merged headers; request values win | Plain records, tuple lists and native Headers locally; omitted headers preserve ordinary requests; inputs remain unchanged | Owning JSDoc | Endpoint-observed headers, not metadata alone |
| Fetch.request URL/method/body and response | Existing implementation; #19436 | Existing dispatch, metadata and rejection contracts retained | String/object URL forms and non-OK responses | Owning JSDoc | Existing metadata/resolution controls plus body/error cases |
| Pipeline App/Data execution | Existing Pipeline and Fetch connection | Plain serializable header configs reach HTTP from both realms | No interceptor machinery required | Test receipt | Real workers and endpoint observation |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Both URL forms send supplied headers; per-request headers override defaults case-insensitively without mutating either input.
- [ ] AC-2: Requests without headers, method/body dispatch, original-URL metadata, response decoding and non-OK rejection envelopes retain their behavior.
- [ ] AC-3: A real App-worker Pipeline and a real Data-worker counterpart deliver the configured header to HTTP; the test observes the outgoing request at the endpoint.

## Out of Scope

Pipeline interceptors and their lifecycle (#9553), broader RequestInit-option support, Xhr/Stream changes, credential storage, token refresh and authentication services.
